title: GPU stability telemetry synthesis and action plan
body:
Summary:

This doc synthesizes recent on-call traces and telemetry from multiple ECC/NVLink/driver-kernel incidents (Nov 2027 window) and proposes a practical, staged action plan: short-term mitigations we can push as runbook changes, medium-term telemetry/alerting improvements, and longer-term architectural hardening. The goal is to reduce noisy correctable-error (CE) cascades, avoid blind evictions, and make graceful fallbacks predictable for latency-sensitive workloads.

Incident snippet (high-level):
- Multiple machines in cluster-gpu-prod experienced rapid CE bursts while running mixed batch/interactive workloads between 2027-11-01 and 2027-11-10.
- Symptoms: intermittent driver OOPS, kernel WARN stack for nvidia, occasional NVLink negotiation failures, and in 3 nodes a kernel panic (call_trace) requiring manual reboot.
- Customer impact: transient timeouts and a handful of request-level stream resets; one Dedicated customer reported degraded throughput for ~12 minutes while we migrated jobs.

Telemetry digest (what we saw):
- ECC metric patterns: CorrectableErrorCount for DRAM channel rose from baseline (~0-2/hr) to 200-400 in a 10–20 minute window. Patterns show bursty spikes often following heavy micro-batch patterns (seq-lens > 2048) and long KV-cache warmups.
- NVLink counters: link_retrain events correlated with ECC bursts on same nodes; negotiation timeouts increased before driver OOPS.
- Kernel log clues: repeated NVRM: Xid (61) and Xid (31) preceding OOPS. Stack traces show nvidia_uvm and nvlink negotiation paths.
- Host-level: no sustained CPU steal; memory pressure low; dmesg shows sporadic pcie AER correctable reports on the same root ports.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Thermal/retimer transient causing NVLink retrain that flips ECC incidents into high-volume correctable errors; retrain loops amplify memory scrubs and driver stack churn.
2) Workload pattern (KV cache + long seq batches) increases sustained write/read to same DRAM banks exposing latent soft error hotspots on affected modules.
3) A specific driver/kernel interaction path triggers a busy-loop in nvlink error handling when combined with repeated retrains, leading to OOPS and eventual kernel panic.

Short-term mitigations (operational — apply within 48 hours):
- Eviction policy tweak: treat nodes with CE bursts > 100 within 15m as "degraded" and trigger a draining window (30–45s) that migrates active interactive sessions off the GPU before full eviction. This avoids hard kill during critical low-latency windows.
- Auto-fence: if NVLink retrain_count > 5 in 10m or link_state_flap, mark NVLink as disabled for scheduling for 10 minutes (force intra-node jobs off cross-link paths).
- Kernel/driver snapshot capture: add an oncall hook to run nvidia-bug-report.sh and copy /var/crash/dmesg when NVRM Xid 31/61 is seen; attach to alert.

Commands to collect evidence (add to runbook):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTILIZATION,PCI | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/params || true
- sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver --since "1 hour ago" | tail -n 200
- sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --output-dir /tmp/bugreport-$(date +%s)
- sudo ethtool -S <pci-device> (for retimer/NVLink link stats)
- sudo dmesg --ctime | egrep -i "NVRM|Xid|nvlink|pci.*AER" > /tmp/gpu-dmesg-$(date +%s).log

Runbook flow (oncall quick steps):
1) Confirm alert vectors: CE-rate alert OR kernel OOPS alert. Note node, job ids, and tenant.
2) Immediately set node to read-only scheduling for interactive traffic (route new requests to warm fallback pool).
3) Run the evidence commands above and attach artifacts to the incident.
4) If retrain_count > 5 and CE burst ongoing, set node to drain and start job moves (do not reboot immediately).
5) If kernel panic occurred or driver OOPS repeats after drain, escalate to oncall lead and schedule cold-reboot with firmware check.

Medium-term telemetry improvements (2–4 weeks):
- New composite alarm: combine "CE burst" + "NVLink retrain" + "NVRM Xid" into a severity-2 alert that auto-creates an incident and pre-populates runbook steps.\- Instrument retrain_count and per-link-flap as custom Prometheus metrics (export via node-exporter plugin or nvml exporter).
- Add a short-lived historical aggregation in our TSDB to look for bank-affinity patterns (same paddr ranges being hit in bursts). This will help validate the workload-hotspot hypothesis.

Longer-term design and hardening (quarter+):
- Firmware/retimer program: partner with hardware vendor to collect retimer traces and attempt retimer firmware update on a small canary pool.
- Driver patch: upstream a defensive sleep/backoff on NVLink retrain loops; add kernel guard to prevent nvlink negotiation from holding GPU driver locks for >5s.
- Automated thermal-aware routing: integrate node thermal telemetry so autoscaler avoids scheduling heavy document/long-seq workloads on nodes with recent NVLink/CE warnings.

Evidence excerpts (obfuscated snippets):
- Example kernel lines (anonymized):
  Nov 09 03:14:12 node-045 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31): GPU has fallen off the bus.
  Nov 09 03:14:13 node-045 kernel: nvlink: link 2: negotiation timeout
  Nov 09 03:14:15 node-045 kernel: PCI AER: First error: type=Corrected, severity=Corrected, 

Open questions to investigate:
- Are CE hotspots matching particular DIMM serials or bank offsets? (hardware lab task)
- Do tenant-specific models or tokenization patterns correlate with bursts? (product/solutions query)
- Is there an environmental correlate (power rail ripple or specific PDU cluster)? (infra telemetry)

Immediate action items (owner, due):
- Priya: push runbook changes and add evidence collection snippets to slack incident template (due 2027-11-16).
- Ethan: implement retrain_count metric export in nvml-exporter and wire to Prometheus (PR by 2027-11-21).
- María: coordinate a 6-node canary firmware test with vendor + lab (plan by 2027-11-30).
- Samir: schedule capacity plan for fallback pool scaling during drain events (due 2027-11-18).

Notes for post-incident writeup: include a timeline from Prometheus event stamps, attach bugreport archives, and a summary table of nodes affected (gpu serial, DIMM ids, firmware version, retrain counts).

Appendix: suggested runbook snippets to copy-paste
- Mark node as degraded (k8s label): kubectl label node NODE gpu-stability=degraded --overwrite
- Drain interactive pods first: kubectl drain NODE --pod-selector=app=interactive --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
- Collect driver logs: sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-bug-report.sh --output-dir /tmp/bug

Closing: This doc is intentionally operational and focused on low-friction mitigations we can roll out in the next two weeks. The telemetry synthesis suggests a multi-causal root cause; we should avoid jumping directly to hardware replacements without the diagnostic matrix above. Feedback welcome — will iterate after the canary firmware test results.

-- Priya (oncall lead, eng-sre)
